explanation: Organ stops switch whole sets of pipes on and off. Pulling every one out at once gives the fullest sound, which is where the phrase 'pull out all the stops' comes from.

claims.text: The pipe organ makes its sound by sending air through pipes, controlled from its keyboards.
The accordion and the harmonium sound through reeds, and the harpsichord plucks strings.
Organ stops turn sets of pipes on and off.
The phrase 'pull out all the stops' comes from drawing all of an organ's stops at once.
